issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares messageOnFeed() as a public abstract method on Animal (indicated by a '+' in the UML), but the reference solution defines it as protected (protected abstract String messageOnFeed()). This visibility mismatch between the specification and the solution can confuse students about the intended visibility and may cause access/override expectations to differ (students may implement it as public following the spec or rely on protected behaviour shown in the solution).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the visibility between specification and implementation. Either (A) change Animal.messageOnFeed() in the solution to be public (public abstract String messageOnFeed()), and ensure all overriding implementations are public, or (B) update the problem statement/UML to indicate protected visibility. Prefer making the method public to match the UML and typical API expectations.

issues.description: The template Farm.java declares the helper method singFarmSongVerse with no Animal parameter (the parameter is commented out: /*Animal animal*/), whereas the problem UML and the reference solution expect singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). This parameter mismatch in the template may mislead students about the method signature they should implement and cause confusion when adapting the provided helper to process each Animal.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template method signature to match the UML and solution: change private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/) to private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) and adjust the method body to use the provided Animal parameter. This makes the template consistent with the specification and the reference solution.
